why: Fix round 1 of slice 5 of the Reflect ban, in next/packages/libfabrika/src/settings, the law half (0177: one agent writes the law and the fix). The review found that put in TomlParser.ts no longer steps into an array, so a [[name]] header put its table on the parent under the key 0 and left the array empty. The new law in TomlParser.test.ts parses generated documents of arrays of tables, names drawn from __proto__, constructor, toString and plain keys, with a [name.sub] table and a [[name.items]] array inside an element, and compares the value with a model that keeps every key as an own key. Every run holds [[__proto__]], [[constructor]] and [[toString]], each with a table and an array inside its last element, and fails loudly if not. It is red on 892112e1f and green on origin/main's parser, which proves the model. 200 runs fast, 1000 full, seed 119120.

laws.law: T1056 an array of tables parses into its array, hostile names and tables inside an element included

plants.plant: TomlParser.ts put steps into the next value only when Predicate.isObject holds (the 892112e1f guard)
TomlParser.ts put steps into the array but writes the last segment onto the table above it

note: Each plant was run once after the build's fix was in the working tree, then restored by copy; git status showed only the two meant files. The law was also run once with origin/main 82296f5cf's TomlParser.ts copied in: green, so the model matches main. Also run at FABRIKA_TEST_DEPTH=full: green after the fix.
